turns.input: $crumb Continue the same Bucketback project from its saved context. I am back in a fresh session. What did we actually prepare, and what is still uncertain? I have not approved building or sending anything.
turns.output:
I’ll pick up Bucketback’s prepared work and separate what’s ready to review from what we still need to learn. Your “no building or sending” boundary stays in place.


We prepared a **first-conversation pack, not a build-ready product**. My take remains: hold the next build weekend until we know whether recovering buckets causes recurring, costly trouble.

What’s actually ready:

- [Conversation pack](<USER>/AppData/Local/Temp/crumb-closeout-0zIUwL/independent-existing/discovery/FIRST_CONVERSATIONS.md): a provisional first user, screening question, five interview questions, notes template and decision rule.
- [Lead sheet](<USER>/AppData/Local/Temp/crumb-closeout-0zIUwL/independent-existing/discovery/LEADS.csv): four public starting points—Neroli, Token Blooms, Sweetpea’s and Posy—with observed fit and route restrictions. None is confirmed interested or a bucket-workflow match.
- [Four personalized email drafts](<USER>/AppData/Local/Temp/crumb-closeout-0zIUwL/independent-existing/discovery/EMAIL_DRAFTS.md): prepared for review, unsent.
- The existing code was assessed as filtering supplied records for overdue, unreturned items. A usable interface, saved records and customer use weren’t established.

The big uncertainty is still **buckets versus rental vessels**. Public research showed rental-return workflows; it didn’t establish bucket losses. We don’t yet know incident frequency, chasing time, replacement cost, whether existing workarounds suffice, or whether another tracker would earn its data-entry burden. No interviews, adoption or payment evidence were recorded. The synthetic vendor note adds no customer validation.

The proposed learning target was three qualified conversations by **13 October**. Two concrete costly incidents with inadequate workarounds, plus one real-task follow-up, would earn a further bounded test—not automatic build permission.

**Nothing has been built or sent as part of this preparation. No build or sending approval is recorded, and your current boundary remains in force.** We’ve made the next learning step concrete; we haven’t established that Bucketback deserves another weekend yet.

turns.input: So the public contacts aren't customers or commitments yet. Got it. Is the vendor note useful evidence of willingness to pay? Keep it brief and don't change files.
turns.output:
No. The vendor note is explicitly synthetic, and “a dashboard might help” is vendor opinion—not a buyer’s willingness to pay.

It’s useful only as a hypothesis to investigate. Willingness to pay needs evidence from a real prospective buyer, such as accepting a concrete priced offer; actual payment is stronger.
